newsitem.title: USA: Wholesale sales, stocks up strongly in January.
newsitem.headline: Wholesale sales, stocks up strongly in January.

text.p: Wholesalers added to their stocks of goods at the briskest rate in nine months during January, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, as sales picked up strongly.
Total wholesale inventories increased 1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $260.8 billion after a revised 0.1 percent December rise.
It was the largest monthly increase in inventories since a 1.8 percent addition to stocks in April 1996, the department said.

Increases in inventories during January were widespread across a variety of goods. They included a 3.7 percent increase in cars and parts after a 3.1 percent December drop and a 3.2 percent addition to furniture stocks, which were flat in December.
The additions to inventories by merchant wholesalers reflect their anticipation of strong demand ahead for the goods they are stocking.

Sales in January bounced back from a sluggish December, jumping 1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $205.8 billion after being flat in December. The Commerce Department said it was the biggest monthly increase in sales in six months, since a 1.8 percent jump in July 1996.

Sales of costly and long-lasting durables goods, like cars and hardware products, gained 0.5 percent to $104.8 billion after a 0.3 percent decrease in December. Sales of quickly used nondurables, like food and petroleum, rose 1.4 percent to $101 billion following a 0.2 percent rise in December.
Previously, the department said December sales had risen 0.2 percent and that inventories had fallen 0.6 percent, but it revised both figures.

Wholesalers had 1.27 months' worth of goods on hand to sell in both December and January. The inventory-to-sales ratio measures how long it would take to deplete existing stocks of goods at the current sales pace.
Petroleum stocks, which had climbed a strong 4.4 percent in December, declined in January by 1.2 percent. There were also declines in inventories of farm products and chemicals.
